name: SWAPP Staking unchecked cToken transferFrom deposit credit
summary: SWAPP's Staking.deposit calls transferFrom on the deposited token without checking its boolean result and credits the caller's staking balance regardless, while emergencyWithdraw pays that balance out for any non-stablecoin token. Compound cTokens signal a failed transferFrom by returning false instead of reverting, so the attacker deposited the Staking contract's entire cUSDC balance without owning any cUSDC, had it credited, and immediately emergency-withdrew the contract's real cUSDC, which backed users' USDC stablecoin deposits.
notes: Staking is an immutable non-proxy contract; its runtime is byte-identical at its creation block and immediately before the exploit, and the unchecked transferFrom is in that runtime.

Exact gross depletion of the Staking contract's cUSDC in the single anchor transaction: receipt log 0x13c transfers 128657759164064 base units (1286577.59164064 cUSDC) from Staking to the attack contract, taking Staking's cUSDC balance from exactly that amount at block 22957532 to zero; no attacker input is involved because the matching deposit transferred nothing. The unit price is cUSDC.exchangeRateStored() at block 22957532 (250283795288235, i.e. 0.0250283795288235 USDC per cUSDC) with USDC at par; the stored rate omits 333 blocks of unaccrued interest, so the value is a marginal floor. A later deposit on 2025-12-22 credited another 57250164371717 cUSDC without a transfer but found no cUSDC left to withdraw, so it adds no loss.

DeFiHackLabs' PoC header links 'Vulnerable Contract Code' to 0x6e90c85a495d54c6d7e1f3400fef1f6e59f86bd6 (ResupplyFi), which is why the coverage matcher associated this lead with the ResupplyFi record; the exploited contract is SWAPP Staking 0x245a551ee0f55005e510b239c917fa34b41b3461 and the episode is unrelated to ResupplyFi.
